title: Grade Calculator
story: Four exams: 85, 92, 78, 95. What's the average? What letter grade? What if the final is worth 40% and each midterm 20%? Grade calculators are the most-requested 'first useful program.' Build one with weighted averages and letter grade mapping.
why: A grade calculator teaches weighted averages, score-to-grade mapping, and struct-based organization — practical student tool and solid programming practice.
analogy: A teacher's gradebook: rows of student names, columns of assignment scores, a final column for the course grade. Your calculator is the formula at the bottom of each column: sum the weighted scores, divide by total weight, map to a letter. The digital gradebook.
try_it: Add weighted scores where each assignment has a different weight (e.g., homework 10%, tests 40%, final 50%). Add GPA calculation on a 4.0 scale. Calculate what score you need on the final to get a B. Add pass/fail threshold.
tips: Always check for division by zero when sum of weights could be 0
Letter grade thresholds: 90=A, 80=B, 70=C, 60=D — standard US scale
common_mistakes: Integer division losing precision in average — (85+92)/2 = 88 not 88.5
Forgetting to sum weights separately — weight total ≠ item count
Mapping exactly 90 to A- or A — define boundary behavior clearly
